summary: The candidate's two advisory-lock regression tests are correct and pass, but the candidate is test-only and overstates the scope of the fix already present on the prepared base. The base had already moved expert_pack_mxfp4 from PyTorch FileBaton to SGLang load_jit/fcntl.flock, which fixes ownerless stale-lock files and dead lock owners. It does not bound a live compiler or kernel stall: a second acquisition still waits indefinitely until an external timeout. The original issue's proposed contract explicitly contained stale shared locks, compiler stalls, and kernel stalls with a bounded process-group timeout and retry. The exact H200 intermittent failure could not be run on the assigned AMD gfx950 system, and the MXFP4 source did not compile under ROCm because cuda_bf16.h is unavailable.

tests.what_was_measured: On the exact prepared base, PyTorch FileBaton remained blocked on a pre-existing ownerless lock file until the external deadline, deterministically reproducing the reported stale-file mechanism.

At exact candidate commit 4f47bef5921d53d3a40186d03225601411530334, all 44 JIT-cache tests passed, including the two added advisory-lock recovery tests. Imports resolved to /job/repo/python/sglang, not an installed SGLang copy.
After SIGKILL of the advisory-lock owner, reacquisition completed in 0.000066 seconds while the .lock path remained, independently confirming dead-owner recovery.
A live holder caused a second _build_lock acquisition to remain blocked until the external deadline; load_jit supplies no bounded wait, process-group kill, or retry for a live compiler stall.
The exact candidate reached hipcc with --offload-arch=gfx950 but failed before kernel execution because expert_pack_mxfp4.cuh includes unavailable NVIDIA header cuda_bf16.h.

gpu_execution_evidence: One AMD Instinct MI355X was visible as gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-. hipcc targeted gfx950, but compilation failed at cuda_bf16.h before an MXFP4 kernel or numerical reference executed.
native_rebuild_evidence: Candidate commit 4f47bef changes only Python tests and report artifacts; it changes no native source or native build input, so no native rebuild was applicable. The cold JIT attempt used the checkout source path and real pinned ROCm compiler.
remaining_counterexamples: While a compiler-owning process remains alive but its compiler child or build call stalls, _build_lock has no timeout and every waiter can remain blocked indefinitely; the independent live-holder test required an external timeout.
The candidate does not add the issue-proposed isolated process group, bounded timeout, fresh TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR/JIT cache, or retry, so it does not contain compiler stalls or kernel stalls.
The candidate regression exercises generic _build_lock directly and does not run the registered MXFP4 test through its JIT path.
The candidate PR body cites https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/757 instead of the required mirror issue https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/839.
remaining_limitations: No NVIDIA H200 was available, so the intermittent H200 CI event was not reproduced statistically or end-to-end.
The assigned gfx950 ROCm environment cannot compile the NVIDIA-specific MXFP4 source because cuda_bf16.h is unavailable; GPU numerical correctness remains unverified.
The historical CI logs establish a hang pattern but do not prove whether each event was an ownerless FileBaton file, a live compiler stall, or a kernel stall.
